state_of_play.narrative: A quiet US session sitting on top of two loud data points. Wall Street was muted into a heavy retail-earnings week - S&P 500 7,772.07 (-0.18%), the Dow off 0.3% at the open, the Nasdaq fractionally higher - but China's July activity data, released this morning, missed across the board: industrial output +4.5% y/y against 4.8% expected and 5.3% in June, retail sales +0.6% against 1.5% expected, fixed-asset investment -6.7% year-to-date and urban unemployment up to 5.2%. The second is closer to home. The UK 30-year gilt yield rose to 5.77% and the 10-year pushed back above 5% as the oil premium revived inflation fears - the Hormuz transmission this desk logged last week as a forecast is now visible in the gilt tape. Brent held $88.78 with the US blockade of Iranian ports open-ended. The AI trade kept its footing regardless: BIS tightened advanced-computing export licensing on 15 Aug to catch subsidiaries whose ultimate parent sits in Country Group D:5, and Nvidia's $500bn financing platform with six large alternative managers marks AI compute being underwritten like grid and toll-road infrastructure. Gold at $4,469 (+2.03%) is still a recovery, about 20% below its 28 January all-time high near $5,600.

crash_risk.read: Still 4 of 7 clusters flashing, and this evening's data added a channel rather than removing one. The benign 12 Aug CPI (+0.1% m/m) and the improved breadth of last week (Russell 2000 record, +3.15%) both stand. Claims at 209k with a 199k four-week average continue to contradict the recession read. What is new is a demand-side crack and a rates-side transmission arriving together: China's July activity missed across the board (output +4.5%, retail sales +0.6%, FAI -6.7% YTD) while the UK 30-year gilt rose to 5.77% and the 10-year back above 5% on oil pass-through. The energy/geopolitical channel is therefore no longer purely prospective - it is now priced in at least one G7 curve. Valuation and concentration remain the hot cluster. Depth risk ~15-25% on a catalyst; timing un-triggered. The 0-100 composite is the 8 Aug weekly figure - the 14 Aug append did not run and is owed.

drivers.oneLiner: The tests landed: capex IS converting to revenue, on both sides of the trade. The discriminator is now contracted/pre-paid backlog, not payer-vs-recipient.
summary: The repricing of the AI tape around who PAYS for capex vs who RECEIVES it - the master factor, now materially revised.
Both payer-neoclouds passed: CRWV rev $2.58bn/+112% with a $104bn backlog; NBIS rev $582m/+454% with positive adj EBITDA and 50-60% customer prepayments.
Revision: fade the SPECULATIVE builder, not the payer. Contracted, pre-paid capacity is being paid for. Invalidation now = a backlog that stops converting, or a capex guide rollover.

investible_themes.read: Promoted from the orphan 'Energy' sector tile to a theme of its own. The premium is no longer a headline risk - it is in the UK curve, with the 30-year gilt at 5.77% and the 10-year back above 5% on oil pass-through.
price: Brent $88.78 (+0.29%), WTI ~$82.40; both +>5% on the week to 14 Aug
flows: Energy sector ratings reversed UW to N across the desk's own sector table
Safe-haven bid showing up in gold alongside crude, same driver
tail: US naval blockade of Iranian ports described as open-ended; Hormuz shut on Iran's terms
UK CPI forecast ~3.5% end-2026 if Hormuz reopens in Q3, materially higher if not (forecast)

access.tradeoff: XLE is equity beta to the premium; USO and BNO track futures, so roll cost means they diverge from spot over any long holding period.
Integrated majors capture the crude move with dividend support, but downstream refining margin partly offsets a spike rather than amplifying it.
Tanker rates rise on rerouting even when volumes fall, which makes tonnage the purest expression of the blockade specifically rather than of the oil price generally.
Shell and BP are sterling LSE lines and the most direct UK route; a Brent ETC gives the commodity without equity risk but carries the same futures roll.

investible_themes.includes: GPU-rental clouds and AI-infra operators renting compute by the hour.
investible_themes.read: The payer layer PASSED its test - both prints converted capex into contracted, largely pre-paid revenue. Financing structure is now the thing to watch, not demand.
flows: Private credit funding GPU fleets at scale
Sovereign & enterprise pre-commitments rising
tail: CRWV backlog $104bn (+246% y/y), FY26 guide $12.4-13.2bn, capex $35-39bn
NBIS: four contracts >$1bn each, 50-60% of associated capex pre-paid

access.tradeoff: Too new and too small a cohort for a dedicated fund; broad AI-infrastructure ETFs hold CRWV at low single-digit weights.
Contracted, prepaid backlog is what re-rated these; they are debt- and prepayment-funded balance sheets, so financing conditions now matter more than demand.
Owns the shell and the credit rather than the rental margin - lower torque to a neocloud re-rating, and the financiers now sit on both sides of the trade.
The purest remaining neocloud exposure is pre-IPO - Crusoe and Lambda are private, reachable only via secondaries or venture funds, and not accessible to most readers.

investible_themes.includes: Uranium miners, enrichment and small-modular-reactor developers.
investible_themes.read: Term price doing the work. Uranium spot $86.36/lb end-July with the long-term contract around $90 - the highest since 2008 and well clear of the <$80 invalidation. Goldman added 46 GW of SMR deployment to 2045 into its model, a 17% uplift to long-run demand.
flows: Dedicated nuclear/uranium ETFs gathering assets
Utility & tech PPAs underwriting new capacity
tail: Uranium term price ~$90/lb - highest since 2008; spot ~$84-86
~9.8 GW committed to datacentres, ~80% not yet in commercial operation

access.tradeoff: URA and URNM are uranium-miner heavy and NLR leans utility; none of the three is an SMR pure-play.
Cameco is the producing anchor; Oklo and NuScale are pre-revenue developers whose value sits in 2030-plus offtake, so the two halves behave nothing alike.
HALEU is the binding constraint into 2027-30, which puts the bottleneck in the fuel cycle rather than in reactor design.
Yellow Cake holds physical U3O8 on the LSE in sterling - the cleanest UK route to the term price (~$90/lb, highest since 2008) without mining or construction risk.

investible_themes.read: Structural demand, full multiples. CrowdStrike and Palo Alto are up roughly 60% and 80% this year and closed at records after Black Hat as AI-agent threat concern broadened the spend case. Palo Alto reports 18 Aug into those multiples.
flows: Software funds overweight security platforms
Steady inflows into cyber-theme ETFs
tail: CRWD FY26 rev $4.81bn (+22%); net-new ARR above $1bn for the first time
AI-driven threat volume lifting budgets; CRWD ~90x, PANW ~55x, ZS ~35x forward

access.tradeoff: Broad coverage of a sector whose two leaders are already up 60% and 80% this year - and the funds are top-heavy in exactly those two.
Both leaders sit at record multiples with near-dated prints - Palo Alto reports 18 Aug and CrowdStrike in early September.
The UCITS wrappers are the practical UK route and hold the same US leaders; Europe's own listed pure-plays thinned out after Darktrace was taken private in 2024.

investible_themes.includes: Prime contractors and munitions — US and European primes.
investible_themes.read: No longer running on stale evidence. Rheinmetall Q2 sales +69.8% to EUR 3.289bn with operating profit +115% and an EUR 80.4bn backlog - but H1 cash flow was -EUR 1.6bn and the shares fell 5.7% on it. The live risk is the theme's own stated kill: a durable Ukraine truce.
flows: Defence & European-defence ETFs seeing steady inflows
UK primes leading on order intake
tail: BAE record GBP84bn backlog; RR raised targets (both carried from July)
New leg: US Navy construction opened to foreign yards with US investment

investible_themes.includes: Industrial, warehouse and surgical robotics plus automation enablers.
investible_themes.read: Autonomy first, and the gap is widening. Waymo is above 500,000 paid rides a week across 11 cities with 3,500 vehicles and a London launch planned for 2026. Tesla's Optimus Gen 3 still has not been shown - Q2 disclosure was that first-generation lines are only being installed.
flows: Automation baskets attracting fresh allocations
Humanoid-robotics venture funding surging
tail: Figure 03 past 1,000 units; AgiBot 15,000 cumulative; ~$4.3bn humanoid funding in 2026
Waymo ~500k paid rides/week across ~10 cities, targeting 1m/week

access.tradeoff: Both leading funds are dominated by legacy factory automation and Japanese industrials - humanoid and robotaxi exposure inside them is close to nil.
Autonomy is the leg with revenue and regulatory approvals, but it arrives inside two megacaps, so the exposure is heavily diluted by everything else they do.
Actuator, sensor and compute suppliers sell to whichever platform wins - but humanoid unit volumes are still measured in thousands, so the revenue is not there yet.
Every humanoid leader is private - roughly $4.3bn went into humanoid startups in 2026 and none of it is reachable on an exchange. This is why the theme reads autonomy-first.
RBOT is the practical UK wrapper, USD-exposed and carrying the same legacy-automation tilt as its US cousins.

investible_themes.includes: Rare-earth miners, processors and magnet makers — inputs to EVs, motors, defence.
investible_themes.read: Materially better evidenced than a week ago. MP's processed rare-earth revenue nearly quadrupled to $94.4m after it stopped sending material to China, with $16.5m from the Texas magnet line - conversion, not just a price pop. China blacklisted MP and USA Rare Earth on 22 June, which cuts both ways.
price: - USA Rare Earth +9% the same day
flows: Dedicated critical-minerals / rare-earth ETFs launching
Government offtake and price-floor support emerging
tail: Section 232 critical-minerals proclamation live; no duties imposed yet
Ten further minerals pulled into the Section 232 net

access.tradeoff: REMX still carries meaningful Chinese-listed weight, which is awkward for a theme whose entire driver is decoupling from China.
MP and USA Rare Earth are both on China's June 2026 export-control blacklist - the policy that supports the thesis is simultaneously an operating constraint.

vehicles: Magnet and separation capacity: MP's Texas line, Neo Performance NEO.TO, Solvay SOLB.BR
access.tradeoff: Processing and magnets are where the West is shortest, so this is the real bottleneck - but capacity is small and lumpy, which makes revenue volatile.
There is no UCITS rare-earth pure-play; a broad mining trust dilutes the signal heavily, so most UK access is via US and Australian lines directly.

investible_themes.includes: Commercial launch, satellites and payload operators.
investible_themes.read: Deteriorated on timeline, not on demand. Rocket Lab's Q4 pad delivery still stands but the company stopped short of reaffirming a first flight before year-end, and coverage now openly contemplates a slip into 2027 - which is the theme's stated kill condition.
price: 13 satellites in orbit, beta targeted by year-end
flows: Early space-theme fund launches gathering assets
Defence primes expanding space exposure
tail: RKLB record backlog $2.36bn (+137% y/y); Q3 guide $250-265m
ASTS $1.30bn backlog, $2.7bn cash, >60 MNO partners

investible_themes.includes: Bitcoin/ether proxies, exchanges and spot ETFs; stablecoin rails.
investible_themes.read: The theme's stated driver has been removed - the CLARITY Act missed its 10 Aug deadline and now likely slips to 2027. Downgraded.
flows: Spot-ETF flows steadier after the surge
Corporate treasuries still adding on dips
tail: CLARITY Act shelved before the August recess; 2026 passage priced ~33-37%
Even on revival, most provisions would not bind until late 2027

access.tradeoff: Direct bitcoin beta with no operating-company risk - and the leg the CLARITY Act stall does not touch, since spot access already exists.
Coinbase carries US market-structure risk directly, which is precisely the driver that has just been removed; MSTR is a leveraged bitcoin proxy rather than an operating business.
UK retail access to crypto ETNs on recognised exchanges opened in October 2025; these are debt securities, not funds, and the underlying is outside FSCS protection.

critLabels: Price + capital flows + tailwind all present
Different from themes already in the book

radar.what: Gate-based and annealing hardware, error correction and quantum-cloud access.
radar.summ: Closest item to promotion. Revenue is now real at the lead name and a basket exists; flows and persistence are the two gaps.
radar.needs: Evidence of fund/ETF flows into the cluster, and price persistence after the June-August drawdown.
evidence: IonQ Q2 rev $80.05m (+287% y/y); FY guide raised to $280-290m
SkyWater acquisition closed 31 July - a vertically integrated stack
Rigetti 108-qubit Cepheus GA on AWS/Azure/QCS; up to $100m CHIPS funding

radar.what: General-purpose humanoids rented per task; fleet operators and enablers.
radar.summ: Deployment numbers arrived but the listed tell keeps slipping - Tesla has still not shown Optimus Gen 3. The leaders are private, so there is no basket. Autonomy, not humanoids, is where this theme is currently investible.
radar.needs: A listed, rentable basket distinct from industrial robotics. Tesla's Gen-3 Optimus reveal is the nearest tell.
evidence: Figure 03 past 1,000 units; AgiBot 15,000 cumulative; Atlas deployments underway
~$4.3bn of humanoid-specific funding within >$8.5bn into robotics startups in 2026
Tesla Optimus Gen 3 still unshown as of mid-Aug; Q2 disclosure was first-gen lines being installed
Every leader remains private - Figure, AgiBot, Physical Intelligence

radar.what: Korean and US yards rebuilding American naval and commercial shipbuilding capacity under new access rules.
radar.summ: NEW this cycle. A dated policy catalyst with an immediate price response and a listed basket - the cleanest new entry in weeks.
radar.needs: Flows confirmation and a second policy or award datapoint; watch whether the two-ship allowance widens.
evidence: US national-security memo (Aug) lets foreign yards with substantial US investment build up to two USN ships at home
Hanwha Ocean +5% on 15 Aug; $100m Philly Shipyard purchase plus a planned $5bn expansion
US Navy RFI to South Korean yards for tankers and destroyers (July)

radar.what: For-profit trade and vocational educators (LINC, UTI, ATGE) riding a skills-gap tailwind.
radar.summ: DEMOTED. The deferred check finally ran and the evidence is negative, not absent - UTI cut its full-year guidance in August.
radar.needs: A UTI guidance reset plus a second strong LINC starts print. Until then the tailwind is real but not converting.
evidence: UTI cut FY26 revenue guidance to $893-900m from $905-915m (Aug 2026)
UTI net income guidance cut to $32-36m from $40-45m
LINC Q4 revenue $142.9m (+19.7% y/y) - the strong datapoint, but it predates the cut

radar.what: Long-duration Treasuries (TLT), quality/low-vol (QUAL, USMV) if the labour turn confirms.
radar.summ: STALLED. The 13 Aug claims print contradicted the turn outright; the July -23k payroll now reads closer to an outlier.
radar.needs: A second soft payroll (early September) AND rising continuing claims. Neither is present.
evidence: Initial claims 209k; four-week average unchanged at 199k, near 1969 lows
Continuing claims fell 22k to 1.777m; insured unemployment rate steady at 1.2%
Counter-signal is on the consumer instead: soft July retail sales, weak sentiment
radar.eta: On hold pending the September payroll

radar.what: On-chain settlement rails, issuers and merchant / FX plumbing.
radar.summ: DEMOTED from graduated. The CLARITY Act - the sole named driver - missed its 10 Aug deadline and was shelved before recess.
radar.needs: Legislative revival, or evidence the rails scale without a US market-structure statute.
evidence: CLARITY Act shelved ahead of the August recess; cloture filed 8 Aug, deadline missed
Prediction markets price 2026 passage at ~33-37%, down from >80% in February
Most operational provisions would not take effect until late 2027 even on revival

radar.what: Private equity, private credit and real assets routed into 401(k) and retail wrappers.
radar.summ: NEW this cycle, and long overdue off the carried list. An August executive order directs regulators to ease private assets into 401(k)s, escalating the March DOL proposal - and the distribution partnerships have already formed.
radar.needs: A price leg - the listed alt managers have not yet re-rated on this - and a final DOL rule rather than a proposal.
evidence: August executive order directs regulators to ease private assets into 401(k)s
DOL rule proposed March 2026 created process-based fiduciary safe harbours
KKR-Capital Group, and Wellington-Vanguard-Blackstone, targeting target-date funds
PwC estimates a 5% alts allocation could unlock >$1tn of AUM by 2030 (estimate)

retired.why: The exit thesis inverted — memory became the cleanest confirmed recipient of AI capex, not a fade.
retired.callTxt: Scored WRONG-ON-THESIS in the 8 Aug weekly; retired 10 Aug (closed, kept for the lesson).
retired.reviveIf: A DRAM/HBM ASP sequential rollover, or CXMT reaching HBM-capable output ahead of the 2028–30 base case.

retired.why: Right on direction (-28% off $142) but the lock-up catalyst is behind it — downgraded to theme-level watch.
retired.callTxt: Scored RIGHT on direction; downgraded from discrete-catalyst to launch-economics theme-watch.
retired.reviveIf: Already folded into the space/launch theme — RKLB Q2 tonight re-prices the launch-economics read.

dormant.why: Parked as fading after three weeks without catalysts - then deployment and regulatory evidence arrived together in August and the drift reversed.
dormant.callTxt: Logged early, parked correctly, revived on dated evidence: Figure 03 past 1,000 units, ~$4.3bn humanoid funding, and Waymo cleared to expand across 18 California counties.
dormant.reviveIf: Already revived - now tracked through the robotics theme and the humanoid-RaaS radar item.

dormant.why: Policy tailwind real but the only listed pure-play (PGNY) guided weak (-22% on print) — not investable.
dormant.callTxt: Logged watch-only, not added. Revisit after 2027 guidance.
dormant.reviveIf: A cleaner investible basket emerges, or PGNY 2027 guidance re-rates the space.

dormant.why: TTD -22% AH on a Q2 miss; H1 already -52% (Publicis dispute, fee-stacking) — idiosyncratic/structural, not an ad-cycle read.
dormant.callTxt: Logged as AVOID to prevent mistaking the drawdown for a value setup.
dormant.reviveIf: A resolution of the structural issues (dispute, fee model) — not on the horizon; do not read as macro.

dormant.why: Inventory glut and a demand air-pocket after the pandemic pull-forward.
dormant.callTxt: Called the 2022 top; re-entered for the AI cycle.
dormant.reviveIf: Already revived — folded into the AI-semiconductor cycle.

dormant.why: Genuinely well funded - CFS $3.94bn raised including $1bn in July 2026, Helion $465m at a $15.5bn valuation - but every leader is private, so there is no investible basket. Recorded so the silence reads as 'private-market only', not 'no news'.
dormant.callTxt: Logged watch-only rather than added. Same posture as the fertility entry.
dormant.reviveIf: A listed pure-play, a fusion-supplier basket with real revenue, or SPARC reaching scientific breakeven (targeted 2027).

signals.headline: China's July activity misses across the board; retail sales +0.6%
summary: Industrial output +4.5% y/y vs 4.8% expected and 5.3% in June
Retail sales +0.6% vs 1.5% expected; fixed-asset investment -6.7% year-to-date
Urban unemployment up to 5.2% from 5.0%, adding pressure for H2 support

signals.headline: UK 30-year gilt yield hits 5.77% as the oil premium reaches the curve
summary: 30-year gilt +10bp to 5.77% on 17 August
10-year back above 5% as the oil surge revived inflation concern
First hard transmission of the Hormuz premium into a G7 curve - previously forecast only

signals.headline: BIS extends advanced-computing licensing to D:5-parented subsidiaries
summary: Guidance issued 15 August 2026
Licences now required regardless of where the subsidiary itself is located
Closes the third-country routing gap; tightens the supply-chain-security driver

signals.headline: MP Materials' processed rare-earth revenue nearly quadruples to $94.4m
summary: Achieved after halting shipments of material to China for processing
Texas magnet operations added $16.5m revenue and $7.5m adjusted profit
China blacklisted MP and USA Rare Earth on 22 June 2026 - support and constraint at once

signals.headline: Rheinmetall Q2 sales +69.8%, backlog EUR 80.4bn, but H1 cash flow -EUR 1.6bn
summary: Operating profit +115%; shares fell 5.7% post-print on the cash outflow, then +5.5% on 16 Aug
Backlog EUR 80.4bn, 70% firm orders - up from the EUR 64bn this desk had carried
Ends three weeks of no fresh European defence evidence

signals.headline: Executive order directs regulators to ease private assets into 401(k)s
summary: Escalates the March 2026 DOL safe-harbour proposal into a White House directive
KKR-Capital Group and Wellington-Vanguard-Blackstone targeting target-date funds
Promoted from the carried list to the radar at 4 of 5

signals.headline: CoreWeave Q2: revenue $2.58bn (+112%), backlog $104bn (+246%)
summary: Adjusted loss $1.03/sh vs $1.22 expected; shares jumped ~13-14% after hours, settling near $105 by Friday.
FY26 guidance raised to $12.4-13.2bn with capex of $35-39bn and adjusted operating income of $960m-1.15bn.
51 active datacentres, 1.5 GW active power, ~3.7 GW contracted; over $25bn of new commitments added early in Q3.
signals.assessment: The master factor's biggest test, and the payer passed - forcing a revision of the fade-the-payer expression.

signals.headline: July CPI benign: +0.1% m/m, 3.4% headline, 2.5% core
summary: Every reading in line with consensus; headline eased from 3.5% and core from 2.6%.
September hike odds fell to ~40% on the day and toward ~30% by 17 Aug after soft retail sales.
Inflation at 3.4% still runs ahead of 3.2% wage growth - a real-income drag, not a policy trigger.
signals.assessment: The timing trigger the desk had flagged resolved benignly; the rate regime is a hold, not a cut.

signals.headline: Nebius Q2: revenue $582m (+454%), adjusted EBITDA positive $236m
summary: EPS -$0.12 against -$0.82 expected; full-year guidance reaffirmed at $3.0-3.4bn revenue.
Four core AI cloud contracts averaging over $1bn each, at $20-25m of yield per megawatt.
Customer prepayments cover 50-60% of the associated capex; contracted-power target lifted to 5 GW.
signals.assessment: Confirms the CoreWeave read: pre-paid, contracted capacity is being funded by customers, not just debt.

signals.headline: Brent $88.52 as the US signals an indefinite blockade of Iranian ports
summary: Brent +1.7% to $88.52 and WTI +1.4% to $82.40 on Friday; both up more than 5% on the week.
US officials flagged measures aimed at the 'economic isolation' of Iran and an open-ended naval blockade.
Hormuz remains shut pending Iranian conditions; ship attacks have continued.
signals.assessment: REVERSES the 10 Aug de-escalation read. This is now the book's main live macro risk and the top UK inflation swing.

signals.headline: Lumentum revenue $1.01bn (+109%) on record 800G, with 1.6T ramping
summary: EPS $3.23 vs $2.97 expected; non-GAAP gross margin crossed 50% ahead of schedule.
Record 800G cloud transceiver shipments; 1.6T production started and ramping through calendar 2027.
Shares rose 14.19% on 12 August.
signals.assessment: Settles the optics demand question - the theme is promoted from building to confirmed.

signals.headline: US-China tariff truce extended 90 days to 10 November
summary: Executive order signed 11 August, one day before the deadline; the 10% reciprocal tariff is preserved.
Without it, rates would have reverted to the 125% reciprocal level.
Negotiations continue on non-reciprocal trade and national-security concerns.
signals.assessment: The reshoring thesis's kill condition did NOT fire - content tariffs stay in place. Thesis-supportive.

signals.headline: Jobless claims 209k with the four-week average at 199k
summary: Initial claims rose 9k to 209k against 202k expected; the four-week average was unchanged.
Continuing claims fell 22k to 1.777m; the insured unemployment rate held at 1.2%.
Claims twice reached their lowest since 1969 this year.
signals.assessment: CONTRADICTS the labour-turn thesis. The radar item is downgraded to stalled; July's -23k now reads as an outlier.

signals.headline: Gold ~$4,414 - a recovery, not a record (ATH ~$5,600 in January)
summary: Spot $4,414.46 on 17 August after a second consecutive weekly gain, having cleared $4,380 on Friday.
The all-time high was set 28 January 2026 near $5,589-5,602, followed by a ~25% correction to ~$4,195 by 12 June.
+10.3% off the 14 July $4,001 call; the Citi $4,500 target stands.
signals.assessment: CORRECTION TO A PRIOR CORRECTION: this desk had logged the ~$5,600 January record as erroneous. It was real.

signals.headline: Cisco AI infrastructure orders reach $9.3bn for FY26, roughly 4.5x
summary: Revenue $17.3bn (+18%) and non-GAAP EPS $1.22 (+23%), both above guidance.
AI infrastructure orders of $4bn in the quarter; FY27 AI infrastructure revenue targeted at $7.5bn.
Shares still fell 4.6% after hours on a heavier hardware mix pressuring gross margin.
signals.assessment: Demand confirmed, but note the pattern: strong AI numbers sold on margin mix at Cisco and AMAT alike.

signals.headline: US opens Navy shipbuilding to foreign yards; Hanwha Ocean +5%
summary: An August national-security memo lets foreign builders with substantial, durable US investment build up to two USN ships at home.
Hanwha bought Philly Shipyard for $100m and has announced a further $5bn of expansion.
Follows a July US Navy RFI to South Korean yards for tankers and destroyers.
signals.assessment: NEW radar entry. A dated policy catalyst with a listed basket and an immediate price response.

signals.headline: CLARITY Act shelved - the crypto rails thesis loses its driver
summary: Cloture was filed 8 August but the 10 August recess deadline passed; passage likely slips to 2027.
Prediction markets price 2026 passage at ~33-37%, down from above 80% in February.
Even on revival, most operational provisions would not bind until late 2027.
signals.assessment: This is the stated invalidation of the crypto market-structure entry. Theme downgraded; stablecoin radar item demoted.

signals.headline: Rocket Lab: record $2.36bn backlog, but Neutron's first flight stays undated
summary: Q2 revenue $234.1m (+62% y/y) with a wider $0.08 loss; the stock fell ~3% to ~$77.70 (worst-case -7% after hours).
Pad delivery still targeted for Q4 2026, but the CEO called the end-year launch window 'narrowing'.
ASTS separately posted revenue of $31.5m, a miss, while holding full-year guidance and reaching 13 satellites in orbit.
signals.assessment: Demand confirmed at both names; the flagship catalyst is not. The theme stays emerging, watch-list sized.

signals.headline: Rare-earth complex rallies: MP +~8%, USA Rare Earth +9%, NioCorp +3%
summary: MP Materials rose to roughly $60 on Friday 14 August.
Traders positioning for further Section 232 and industrial-policy support for domestic processing.
The January critical-minerals proclamation imposed no duties yet but ten more minerals have since been pulled in.
signals.assessment: Price leadership within the cluster - the first of the five signals to fire here in weeks.

signals.headline: Rotation leadership flips to Asia: Nikkei +4.7%, Europe stalls
summary: Nikkei 225 +4.74% and TOPIX +3.00% on the week; Korea strong on semiconductors.
STOXX 600 -0.04% ended a four-week winning streak; FTSE 100 -0.56%, its first weekly decline in five.
Russell 2000 +3.15% to a fresh record - breadth broadening in the US too.
signals.assessment: The ex-US thesis holds but its leadership rotated. The prior Europe-led framing is now stale.

signals.headline: Google overhauls DeepMind leadership; Hassabis to chairman, Jeff Dean exits
summary: Announced 5 August: Koray Kavukcuoglu elevated to lead Gemini's direction; Hassabis moves to chairman and Alphabet chief scientist.
Chief scientist Jeff Dean leaves after 27 years to start a company, taking colleagues with him.
Alphabet fell ~4% on the day, with Gemini 3.5 Pro reported months behind schedule.
signals.assessment: CLOSES a long-running unverified trace. Model-leadership risk at one hyperscaler, not an AI-capex signal.

signals.headline: CrowdStrike and Palo Alto hit record highs after Black Hat
summary: Zscaler rose about 5% alongside; analysts lifted CrowdStrike's target to $237.
CrowdStrike FY26 revenue $4.81bn (+22%) with net-new ARR above $1bn for the first time.
Multiples are full: CRWD ~90x, PANW ~55x, ZS ~35x forward.
signals.assessment: A quietly strong week for a carried theme; structural spend confirmed, valuation the constraint.
